description: Building SPHEREx Time Machine: a live web tool that streams real NASA SPHEREx data, blinks epochs to spot moving objects, and generates spectra on the fly. Python/Streamlit + astropy, proper-motion correction, variance-weighted differencing, Discovery Mode mover ranking. Validated on all five NASA test targets, deployed publicly. Seeking: front-end polish, demo video editing, science communication, data-viz. If you can make real NASA data feel magical, join us!
summary:
We developed the SPHEREx Time Machine, a public, login-free web application that transforms NASA’s SPHEREx archive into an interactive time-series dashboard. To address the challenge of finding moving objects hidden in massive datasets, the app allows users to enter any sky coordinates and instantly "blink" through real Level-2 infrared epochs. It uses HTTP Range requests to stream FITS files directly from NASA's AWS Open Data mirror in real-time.

Beyond simple blinking, we built a Discovery Mode that automatically ranks moving candidates and an on-the-fly spectrum generator using the per-pixel WCS-WAVE data.

This tool is important because SPHEREx will image over a billion objects, and no single team can sift through that alone. By providing a mobile-friendly, embeddable interface that runs entirely on live NASA data, we empower students, volunteers, and researchers to hunt for new comets, asteroids, and brown dwarfs—turning the classic 1930s photographic blink comparator into a modern, browser-based discovery engine.
details:
The SPHEREx Time Machine allows users to enter Right Ascension and Declination to instantly view a "blink" of real SPHEREx Level-2 infrared data. It streams raw FITS data directly from AWS Open Data using HTTP Range requests, avoiding 71MB file downloads. Users can switch between single-band or all-band coadds, view per-pixel wavelengths, and generate on-the-fly spectra by clicking on stars. It features a "Discovery Mode" that runs source detection across epochs and ranks moving objects by displacement and uncertainty, along with variance-weighted difference imaging to subtract two epochs.

Benefits & Impact: SPHEREx will image over a billion objects. The intended impact is to democratize discovery. By providing a browser-based tool that requires no Python, no login, and no massive data downloads, we empower students, citizen scientists, and researchers to actively hunt for moving objects (comets, asteroids, brown dwarfs) without needing a supercomputer.

Tools & Languages Used: Python, Streamlit, Astropy (FITS/WCS), Astroquery, AWS S3 (nasa-irsa-spherex), Photutils (DAOStarFinder), Plotly, Pandas, GitHub Codespaces (for 16GB RAM hosting).

How it is creative: We bypassed traditional API bottlenecks by writing a custom HTTP Range reader to parse FITS headers and pull only the pixel cutouts needed. We also utilized the SPHEREx Linear Variable Filter (LVF) by reading the WCS-WAVE extension, allowing us to build real near-infrared spectra from multiple revisits on the fly, rather than just displaying static images.

Factors considered: We built a fallback for NASA's IRSA 502 outage by reconstructing S3 URLs and serving cached real metadata. We handled proper-motion correction (essential for fast movers like Barnard's Star) and propagated contamination flags and variance maps to ensure scientific validity.
